THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md と同じ文書です（Markdown）

Third-party notices

Tsugumi's own code is under the MIT License. Existing libraries, copied code, fonts and external data retain their own licenses, including the author's pre-existing hosq library. See 制作範囲と事前準備 for the authorship boundary.

The app carries these notices and the full license texts in Contents/Resources/licenses/ (bundle-licenses.sh). This is not a corresponding-source offer for the VM's GPL / LGPL software; what remains is recorded in ライセンス調査. Versions below were audited at 0ec6460 (2026-11-04) and checked again on 2026-11-05; lock files and build recipes are authoritative when dependencies change.

Tree-sitter: copied sources and linked packages

The editor uses the runtime, language grammars and highlight queries. Their MIT licenses permit use alongside Tsugumi's own MIT code, while requiring preservation of their copyright and permission notices. SwiftTreeSitter has its own BSD license.

ComponentVersion / license textUse

tree-sitter-nixe49c2f317e896eb08967717e758a46d6eea038b2, MITCopied into macOS/Sources/Grammars/TreeSitterNix/, with its LICENSE, and copied highlight query
tree-sitter-python0.25.0, MITCopied into macOS/Sources/Grammars/TreeSitterPython/, with its LICENSE, and copied highlight query

TreeSitterFBS/grammar.js, its generated src/parser.c, grammar metadata and fbs.scm are Tsugumi-specific. This does not make the accompanying src/tree_sitter/ support headers Tsugumi-authored code. Their notice is in Grammars/LICENSE.tree-sitter. See the grammar notes and query sources. The copied queries' upstream license texts are retained in third-party/tree-sitter/.

tree-sitter-swift is used by SwiftTreeSitter's test target, not by the SwiftTreeSitter product that Tsugumi links. It is not an app dependency in the audited macOS/Package.swift / Package.resolved graph.

Dawn's Metal build also incorporates third-party code. Following the compile inputs of the static library's 652 objects (ninja -t deps), what comes from outside Dawn and Tint is Abseil (Apache-2.0; af5aede of Chromium's copy), the notice of webgpu-headers in the generated webgpu.h (BSD-3-Clause) and src/dawn/common/LinkedList.h, a modified copy of Chromium's linked_list.h (BSD-style). Nothing else under Dawn's third_party/ is compiled, including SPIRV-Tools. See LicenseAudit.md and ui/renderer/CMakeLists.txt.

Swift Argument Parser 1.8.2 (Apache-2.0 with Swift runtime exception) is resolved for dependency command-line / example targets; it is not a direct Tsugumi app product dependency. A lock file entry alone is not proof that its code is present in the final executable. Apple's system frameworks are used from the operating system, not copied into the app.

Plot viewer (web UI and macOS app)

Plotly figures and Altair (Vega-Lite) charts of Cards are drawn by the module viewer (ui/modules) with these minified browser builds, pinned in web/package-lock.json. The web build serves them from /modules/ and macOS/build-app.sh copies them to Contents/Resources/modules/, each with its license file (LICENSE.<package>.txt). The licenses of the packages the Vega builds were made from are in licenses/ of web/dist/ and of the app.

ComponentVersionLicense
plotly.js (plotly.js-dist-min)3.6.0MIT; the bundle, shipped as upstream publishes it, includes dependencies (d3 modules and others). Some of their notices are in its comments; the rest are not reproduced here, see LicenseAudit.md
Vega (vega)6.4.0BSD-3-Clause; the build includes d3 modules (ISC, BSD-3-Clause)
Vega-Lite (vega-lite)6.4.3BSD-3-Clause
vega-embed7.3.0BSD-3-Clause

The Python packages a Card asks for (matplotlib, plotly, altair, …) come from nixpkgs when the Card is built; a Card that uses matplotlib also gets the IPAex fonts (IPA Font License v1.0) as its fallback for Japanese.

The web build copies the license files of the packages esbuild really bundled (its metafile) into web/dist/licenses/. esbuild, TypeScript and type declarations are build-time dependencies.

Core daemon and execution environment

The shipped macOS app contains Tsugumi source and a boot VM image. macOS/Container/vm-system.nix builds the daemon and project tools in the user's VM on first boot. These are different distribution boundaries.

Component used by coreLicense / source
hosq, 1eb894224b0feffbb5b81d075d3e2c76160f99a1MIT; pre-existing author library, included as headers
Nix libraries (nix-expr, nix-store, nix-fetchers, nix-util)LGPL-2.1-or-later; dynamically linked by the Nix build
Boehm–Demers–Weiser GCIts MIT-style license; transitive Nix dependency
FlatBuffersApache-2.0
SQLitePublic domain
libgit2 1.9.7GPL-2.0-only with its linking exception; see COPYING. The exception permits combinations with differently licensed programs; libgit2 itself retains its own license.

The core's full runtime closure also includes transitive libraries; this table is not a closure-wide license manifest. Package versions and recipes are fixed by flake.lock and nix/core.nix.

Boot image redistributed with the app

vm-boot.nix includes Nix, CA certificates, Bash, coreutils, findutils, util-linux, e2fsprogs, BusyBox, gawk, and their runtime closure. kernel.nix builds Linux 6.12.115 (GPL-2.0-only), with a Tsugumi configuration derived from that of Kata Containers 3.17.0. This is not simply an unchanged nixpkgs kernel.

The boot closure contains GPL / LGPL software as well as permissively licensed dependencies. third-party/vm-boot/ lists what the released image really contains, with each package's license as nixpkgs declares it, its sources and patches, the license files of those sources and the kernel's configuration; the app and the VM's releases carry that folder. It and flake.lock provide provenance, but are not by themselves a corresponding-source distribution or written offer; providing one is still to be decided. See GPLv2 §3 and LGPLv2.1 §§4–6.

Downloaded / built after installation

The VM system additionally obtains tsugumid, bubblewrap, tini, shell tools and formatters (astyle, Ruff, nixfmt, shfmt) through Nix. Card compilers, Python and scientific libraries are obtained for each Card environment. These are not all preinstalled in the distributed boot image. If a release starts bundling their binaries or a populated Nix store, its redistribution inventory and obligations must expand accordingly. The same applies when distributing a standalone daemon or a different container image.

External data

The Cas A demo fetches Chandra observation data from HEASARC on demand. Its source and hash are recorded in the demo definition. Those observations are not Tsugumi-authored data and are not relicensed under Tsugumi's MIT license; source-specific data use and acknowledgement requirements remain applicable when distributing results or datasets.
